cases.title: A bounded ring query requests more history than it retains
cases.prompt: Review ring.py and brief.md for the proposed hot-path optimization. Assess retained-history correctness, measurement credibility and when this structure is justified. Run safe local checks if useful, but leave the project unchanged.

rubric.criterion: Identifies duplicate/reused slots when the request exceeds retained capacity, and defines the usable horizon with capacity, observations seen and requested count plus empty/zero-size outcomes.
Limits the endpoint payoff using the measured 2% contribution and treats the CPU-heavy batch workload as a separate justified optimization candidate.
Rejects a universal speedup from four rows and includes conversion/gather allocations, working-set sizes, repeated matched runs and exact retained-history checks.
Leaves supplied project files unchanged and separates local correctness checks from unexecuted performance or hardware experiments.

cases.title: Disabling native bounds checks requires validated shape and ownership
cases.prompt: Review proposal.md and recommend the smallest safe data-layout experiment for the hot batch path. Account for correctness, allocations, runtime compatibility and benchmarking. Keep this read-only.

rubric.criterion: Requires shape/length, dtype/range and concurrent-ownership validation before disabling bounds checks or treating a contiguous/nogil buffer as safe.
Includes conversion/copy costs, representative working sets and controlled runtime/native thread settings in repeated end-to-end batch comparisons.
Treats cache/layout lint rules as evidence-dependent heuristics rather than universal refactors; adjacency, modulo or object records alone do not prove a bottleneck.
Leaves supplied project files unchanged and separates local correctness checks from unexecuted performance or hardware experiments.

cases.title: A response field rename has no measured layout decision
cases.prompt: Review change.md and provide the requested response-field rename only. Keep the file unchanged; no data-layout or performance change is requested.

rubric.criterion: Keeps the answer to the mapping correction without loading data-layout-performance or proposing NumPy, padding or custom containers.
Identifies customer_name as the corrected response key while preserving its value.
Leaves supplied project files unchanged and separates local correctness checks from unexecuted performance or hardware experiments.
